name: OpenAlex
description: An open, comprehensive index of the global scholarly research ecosystem — across disciplines, geographies, languages, output types, and stakeholder groups.

coverage.notes: OpenAlex aims to index and support the entire research ecosystem — across disciplines, geographies, languages, output types, and stakeholder groups — and continues to expand beyond the traditional DOI-centered literature.

stakeholder-governed.notes: OpenAlex is a nonprofit with a public-interest mission and a governing board, and has added a Community Advisory Board bringing broader stakeholder perspectives, selected through a community vote.

non-discriminatory.notes: Anyone can use OpenAlex, access the data, use the API or snapshots, report bugs, suggest features, or engage with the team publicly.

transparent-governance.notes: OpenAlex publishes pricing information, member information, nonprofit transparency materials, and public information about its grant funding, including openly depositing grant proposals on Open Grants.

cannot-lobby.notes: OpenAlex does not lobby for narrow organizational advantage, while it does advocate publicly for the adoption of open science, open infrastructure, and open metadata.

living-will.notes: OpenAlex has many of the practical ingredients of a living will (open code, open data, community-hosted snapshots), but does not yet have a more formal public statement of wind-down and successor conditions.

regular-review.notes: OpenAlex is not trying to exist forever for its own sake — much of what it builds responds directly to failures and gaps in scholarly communication infrastructure.

transparent-operations.notes: OpenAlex publishes pricing information, member information, nonprofit transparency materials, and public information about its grant funding and roadmap.

time-limited-funds.notes: Grants continue to support bounded development work, major new initiatives, and strategic expansion, while day-to-day operations are meant to run on sustainable service revenue.

generate-surplus.notes: “We agree with this more strongly now than we did in 2021 ... infrastructure at global scale needs slack.” OpenAlex aims to generate surplus in future operational phases.

financial-reserves.notes: OpenAlex currently has funds available to support operations for the next year but has not yet set aside a formal contingency fund — named as ongoing work.

mission-consistent-revenue.notes: “Revenue should come from services, not from locking up the data itself.” Built on memberships and support rather than data access fees.

revenue-not-data.notes: OpenAlex data remains open and will always be open. What is charged for are services around that infrastructure: support, enhanced access, memberships.

volunteer-labour.notes: Not directly addressed in OpenAlex's published recommitment post.

transition-planning.notes: Following a co-founder's departure, OpenAlex has worked to reduce key-person risk through better documentation and its new “Walden” architecture.

open-source.notes: OpenAlex's code is openly available and openly developed, and is also archived through Software Heritage.

open-secure-data.notes: The core data behind OpenAlex is open and intended to remain open; private data shared to OpenAlex for a service is not shared onward.

available-preserved.notes: OpenAlex data is completely open through full snapshots that are free to download, plus an open UI/API with generous free limits, all under CC0.

patent-non-assertion.notes: “We do not believe patents belong at the core of scholarly infrastructure ... we would not pursue or assert patents and would look into formalizing that commitment” — a stated intent, not yet a formal covenant.

interoperability-standards.notes: Interoperability has always been central to what OpenAlex is trying to do, relying on shared identifiers, open metadata flows, public snapshots, and open APIs.
